rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report places the beast's emergence when goodness ends, no one enjoins right or forbids wrong, and no repentant or deputy remains.
rows.anchor: وروي أن خروجها حين ينقطع الخير، ولا يؤمر بمعروف، ولا ينهى عن منكر، ولا يبقى منيب ولا نائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith lists the beast and the sun rising in the west among the first portents, without specifying which comes first; the sun's rising appears to be the last portent.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: «أن الدابة وطلوع الشمس من المغرب من أول الأشراط»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading is that one beast emerges; a report instead has a beast in every land, making the word a generic noun.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الدابة التي تخرج هي واحدة. وروي أنه يخرج في كل بلد دابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conflicting accounts about the beast's nature, appearance, place, number, size, actions, and attributes contradict one another, so he omits them as unreliable and wasteful.
rows.anchor: اختلافا مضطربا معارضا بعضه بعضا، ويكذب بعضه بعضا فاطرحنا ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading with a doubled consonant means that the beast speaks; readings by Ubayy and others support the sense of informing or speaking.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: تكلمهم، بالتشديد، وهي قراءة الجمهور، من الكلام ويؤيده قراءة أبي: تنبئهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The beast tells people that all religions besides Islam are false.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: تكلمهم ببطلان سائر الأديان سوى الإسلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported explanation is that the beast addresses each person, identifying the believer as a believer and the unbeliever as an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نخاطبهم، فتقول للمؤمن: هذا مؤمن، وللكافر: هذا كافر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وابن جبير، وأبو زرعة، والجحدري، وأبو حيوة، وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: A group of readers uses the lightened form, and another reading has the beast wound people, supporting an interpretation from the root meaning a wound.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وابن جبير، وأبي زرعة، والجحدري، وأبي حيوة، وابن أبي عبلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In reply to Abu al-Hawra, Ibn Abbas says the beast does both: it speaks to the believer and wounds the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وسأل أبو الحوراء ابن عباس: تكلم أو تكلم؟ فقال: كل ذلك تفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the beast brands the unbeliever's forehead and wipes the believer's face, making it white.
rows.anchor: وروي: أنها تسم الكافر في جبهته وتربده، وتمسح على وجه المؤمن فتبيضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ between opening the hamza in the phrase about people, using a prefixed bāʾ, and the majority's kasra; the kasra can introduce God's speech or the beast's speech, though the following phrase favors God's speech.
rows.anchor: فاحتمل الكسر أن يكون من كلام الله، وهو الظاهر لقوله: بآياتنا، واحتمل أن يكون من كلام الدابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the kasra, the clause can be parsed with an implied verb of saying or by treating the beast's speech like the direct address, and the bāʾ can be understood through ellipsis or divine association.
rows.anchor: وكسرت إن هذا على القول، إما على إضمار القول، أو على إجراء تكلمهم إجراء تقول لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the fatha, the expressed or implied bāʾ attaches to the beast's speech; it may also be causal, since they did not believe God's signs.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه متعلق بتكلمهم، أي تخاطبهم بهذا الكلام. ويجوز أن تكون الباء المنطوق بها أو المقدرة سببية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in this act benefit believers through reflection, so they are singled out even though the signs are available to others too.
rows.anchor: لما كان لا ينتفع بالفكر في هذه الآيات إلا المؤمنون، خصوا بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blowing in the trumpet is the blast of terror.
rows.anchor: وهذه النفخة هي نفخة الفزع

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports three blasts: worldly terror, which is not the greatest terror; the blast of swooning; and the blast of rising from the graves.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة أن الملك له في الصور ثلاث نفخات: نفخة الفزع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view counts two blasts by combining terror and swooning, citing the verse that says the trumpet is blown again.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نفختان، جعلوا الفزع والصعق نفخة واحدة، واستدلوا بقوله: ثم نفخ فيه أخرى

rows.speaker: صاحب الغنيان
rows.claim: The phrase about the trumpet being blown refers to resurrection from the graves and gathering.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب الغنيان: ويوم ينفخ في الصور للبعث من القبور والحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense description of future terror signals that its occurrence is certain.
rows.anchor: وعبر هنا بالماضي في قوله: ففزع، وإن كان لم يقع إشعارا بصحة وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use of a past verb for a future event is also illustrated by the statement that Pharaoh's people are led to the Fire after the verse says he will lead his people on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: بعد قوله: يقدم قومه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies those spared from terror as Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death.
rows.anchor: فقال مقاتل: هم جبريل، وميكائيل، وإسرافيل، وملك الموت

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies those spared from terror as the houris, keepers of Hell, and bearers of the Throne.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: الحور العين، وخزنة النار، وحملة العرش

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir includes Moses among those spared because Moses had once been struck unconscious.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر: منهم موسى، لأنه صعق مرة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra identifies them as martyrs and transmits a prophetic report that they are alive and provided for with their Lord.
rows.anchor: ورواه أبو هريرة حديثا، وهو: «أنهم هم الشهداء عند ربهم يرزقون»

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr also identifies them as martyrs carrying swords around the Throne.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن جبير، قال: هم الشهداء متقلدو السيوف حول العرش

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies those spared as believers, citing the statement that they are safe from that day's terror.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم المؤمنون لقوله: وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars say no sound report identifies those spared, leaving all proposed identifications possible.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العلماء: ولم يرد في تعيينهم خبر صحيح، والكل محتمل

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the scholar missed Abu Hurayra's hadith; Ibn al-Arabi authenticated it, making that report decisive while the other identifications remain conjectures.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبي: خفي عليه حديث أبي هريرة، وقد صححه القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars take the trumpet blast literally, while another view treats it as a metaphor for summoning the dead; he prefers the literal sense because Quranic usage and sound hadith repeatedly mention the trumpet.
rows.anchor: والأول قول الأكثرين، وهو الصواب، لكثرة ورود النفخ في الصور في القرآن وفي الحديث الصحيح

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats God's making as an emphatic verbal noun whose omitted confirmer governs the preceding Judgment-Day clause and means rewarding the righteous and punishing sinners.
rows.anchor: وجعل هذا الصنع من جملة الأشياء التي أتقنها وأتى بها على الحكمة والصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses God's making as a verbal noun confirming the preceding circumstantial clause: God made the mountains move by removing them from the earth and making them pass like clouds.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أن صنع الله مصدر مؤكد لمضمون الجملة السابقة، وهي جملة الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects al-Zamakhshari's double ellipsis: an emphatic verbal noun cannot lose both its governing verb and the clause whose meaning it confirms, since deletion undermines emphasis.
rows.anchor: فذلك لا يصح، لأن المصدر المؤكد لمضمون الجملة لا يجوز حذف جملته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further parsing makes the verbal noun an exhortation meaning: look at God's making.
rows.anchor: وقيل: انتصب صنع الله على الإغراء بمعنى، انظروا صنع الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari praises the passage's arrangement as tightly connected and says the emphatic verbal noun testifies to the truth of what precedes it.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا المصدر، إذا جاء عقيب كلام، جاء كالشاهد لصحته، والمنادي على سداده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He criticizes al-Zamakhshari's ornate expansion as twisting Quranic wording to support Mu'tazilite doctrine.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكر من شقاشقه وتكثيره في الكلام، واحتياله في إدارة ألفاظ القرآن لما عليه، من مذاهب المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two Basran readers and Ibn Kathir read the verb in the third person; the other canonical readers use second-person address.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العربيان، وابن كثير: يفعلون بالياء وباقي السبعة بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good deed means faith; Ibn Abbas, al-Nakha'i, and Qatada specifically identify it as the declaration that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: والحسنة: الأيمان. وقال ابن عباس، والنخعي، وقتادة: هي لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: الحسن، وابن جريج، وعكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj, and Ikrima take the reward as a good whose origin and growth come from the good deed, rather than as a comparative.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن، وابن جريج، وعكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He holds that خير is not comparative and من marks the starting point: the deed produces a reward, which is itself a good.
rows.anchor: ويظهر أن خيرا ليس أفعل تفضيل، ومن لابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says nothing is better than the declaration that there is no god but God, supporting the non-comparative reading.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: ليس شيء خيرا من لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes خير as comparative: the deed ends while its multiplied reward lasts, and the servant's act differs greatly from the master's.
rows.anchor: فقال الزمخشري: فله خير منها، يريد الإضعاف، وأن العمل ينقضي والثواب يدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although scholars dispute the construction meaning that there is a great difference between servant and master, he considers it permissible.
rows.anchor: والصحيح جوازه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows the comparative reading by supplying an omitted noun: God grants more than the deed's measure and what it deserves.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: يحتمل أن يكون للتفضيل، ويكون في قوله: منها، حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says one good deed earns tenfold reward; this explanation requires comparison because a deed and its reward cannot otherwise be compared.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: يعطى بالواحدة عشرا، والداعية إلى هذا التقدير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the reward as the necessary knowledge of the afterlife replacing earthly acquired knowledge, together with the pleasure of seeing God's noble face.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ثواب المعرفة الحاصلة في الدنيا هي المعرفة الضرورية الحاصلة في الآخرة، ولذة النظر إلى وجهه الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest felicity is the pleasure of seeing God; otherwise eating and drinking would have to rank above knowing God.
rows.anchor: ولو لم تحمل الآية على ذلك، لزم أن يكون الأكل والشرب خيرا من معرفة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ between an indefinite, tanwin reading of min faza and an iḍāfa to the time expression; on the tanwin reading, that expression can modify safe or terror, or describe the terror.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون: من فزع، بالتنوين، ويومئذ، منصوب على الظرف معمول لقوله: آمنون، أو لفزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the iḍāfa reading, the Arabs, Ibn Kathir, and Isma'il from Nafi' kasra the mīm, while Nafi' in another transmission has the built form with fatha.
rows.anchor: فكسر الميم العربيان، وابن كثير، وإسماعيل بن جعفر، عن نافع، وفتحها، بناء لإضافته إلى غير متمكن نافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin in يومئذ compensates for an omitted clause, preferably the nearby clause about the one who came with a good deed, though other nearby Judgment-Day clauses are possible.
rows.anchor: والتنوين في يومئذ تنوين العوض، حذفت الجملة وعوض منها، والأولى أن تكون الجملة المحذوفة ما قرب من الظرف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says min faza may denote one terror or many because it is a verbal noun; the plural sense can encompass every terror of Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي ما معناه: من فزع، بالتنوين، أو بالإضافة، ويجوز أن يراد به فزع واحد، وأن يراد به الكثرة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari distinguishes an initial sudden terror felt by everyone from fear of punishment; the righteous can feel the first while remaining safe from harm.
rows.anchor: الفزع الأول: ما لا يخلو منه أحد عند الإحساس بشدة نفع، وهو يفجأ من رعب وهيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil deed means unbelief and sins by those whom God has decreed, under His will, to enter Hell.
rows.anchor: والسيئة: الكفر والمعاصي ممن حتم الله عليه من أهل المشيئة بدخول النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faces are singled out because they are the noblest limbs; throwing them face-first entails throwing the whole person, or face stands for the whole person as head and neck do.
rows.anchor: وخصت الوجوه، إذ كانت أشرف الأعضاء، ويلزم من كبها في النار كب الجميع

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says those cast face-first into Hell are thrown upside down, their heads first.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو العالية، أعلاهم قبل أسفلهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak takes the phrase as a figurative way of saying that they are thrown into the Fire.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك كناية عن طرحهم في النار، قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether they are being repaid is addressed to them through an implied saying at the moment they are cast into Hell.
rows.anchor: هل تجزون: خطاب لهم على إضمار القول، أي يقال لهم وقت الكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophet's command comes from God through Gabriel, or from rational proof of God's oneness; worship means singling God out without a partner, unlike Quraysh.
rows.anchor: والآمر هو الله تعالى على لسان جبريل، أو دليل العقل على وحدانية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protected town is Mecca, and attributing its sanctification to God honors it and marks its special status.
rows.anchor: والبلدة: مكة، وأسند التحريم إليه تشريفا لها واختصاصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no conflict between God's sanctifying Mecca and the reports that Abraham sanctified Mecca and Muhammad sanctified Medina: divine attribution refers to decree and foreknowledge, while the prophets' attribution refers to prayer, appearance, and proclamation.
rows.anchor: لأن إسناد ذلك إلى الله من حيث كان بقضائه وسابق علمه، وإسناده إلى إبراهيم من حيث كان ظهور ذلك بدعائه ورغبته وتبليغه لأمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca's safety from raids and upheavals is a favor to Quraysh, and God destroyed those who sought to harm it.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: حرمها، تنبيه بنعمته على قريش، إذ جعل بلدتهم آمنة من الغارات والفتن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read الذي as an adjective of the Lord, while Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas read التي as an adjective of the town.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود، وابن عباس: التي حرمها: صفة للبلدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning God's ownership of Mecca, the text states that all things belong to Him, including the town within His universal lordship.
rows.anchor: ولما أخبر أنه مالك هذه البلدة، أخبر أنه يملك كل شيء فقال: وله كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among Muslims means surrendering and obeying God's command, or remaining among the monotheists steadfast in Islam, as named in another verse.
rows.anchor: أو من الحنفاء الثابتين على ملة الإسلام المشار إليهم في قوله: هو سماكم المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to recite the Quran most naturally means reciting it to the audience, since the following division fits recitation; it may instead mean following the Quran.
rows.anchor: وأن أتلوا القرآن، إما من التلاوة، أي: وأن أتلو عليكم القرآن، وهذا الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to whoever strays is omitted because the parallel response is understood; alternatively the warning phrase contains an implied pronoun linking it to the conditional, and guidance belongs to God.
rows.anchor: وحذف جواب من ضل لدلالة جواب مقابله عليه، أو يقدر في قوله: فقل إنما أنا من المنذرين ضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to praise God thanks Him for granting the Prophet the honor of prophethood, messengership, and a lofty station.
rows.anchor: فيحمد ربه على ما خصه به من شرف النبوة والرسالة، واختصه من رفيع المنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise to show signs threatens the enemies with signs that will compel them to recognize them as God's signs.
rows.anchor: تهديد لأعدائه بما يريهم الله من آياته التي تضطرهم إلى معرفتها والإقرار أنها آيات الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the signs will appear in the afterlife, when recognition can no longer benefit them.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: وذلك في الآخرة حتى لا تنفعهم المعرفة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi places the signs in this life, including smoke, the splitting of the moon, and punishments inflicted on the people.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: في الدنيا وهي الدخان وانشقاق القمر وما حل بهم من نقمات الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other proposed times or signs are the Battle of Badr and the beast's emergence, even if it occurs later.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يوم بدر. وقيل: خروج الدابة، ولو بعد حين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes God's signs as those in people and in the rest of creation, as in the verse about signs on the horizons and within themselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل: آياته في أنفسكم وفي سائر ما خلق مثل قوله: سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs may be the Prophet's miracles, attributed to God because He performs and displays them through His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معجزات الرسول، وأضافها إليه لأنه هو مجريها على يدي رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will recognize the signs' reality and will have no room to deny them.
rows.anchor: فتعرفونها: أي حقيقتها، ولا يسعكم جحودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority use third-person plural in عما يعملون, shifting from direct address to report; Nafi and Ibn Amir read second-person to match سيريكم.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: عما يعملون، بياء الغيبة، التفاتا من ضمير الخطاب إلى ضمير الغيبة

none: This segment contains verse text only, with no commentary.
This segment contains verse text only, with no commentary.
This segment contains verse text only, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitab refers to the Quran; al-Hawfi parses تنزيل as a subject and لا ريب as its predicate, while other grammarians offer several alternative clause structures.
rows.anchor: والكتاب: القرآن. قال الحوفي: تنزيل مبتدأ، ولا ريب خبره

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses الم as subject, تنزيل as its predicate meaning revealed, and لا ريب فيه as a circumstantial clause attached to the book through تنزيل; he also gives other possible attachments and predicate arrangements.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: الم مبتدأ، وتنزيل خبره بمعنى المنزل، ولا ريب فيه حال من الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers تنزيل as the subject, لا ريب as an interjection, and من رب العالمين as the predicate.
rows.anchor: والذي أختاره أن يكون تنزيل مبتدأ، ولا ريب اعتراض، ومن رب العالمين الخبر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya attaches من رب العالمين to تنزيل, requiring fronting and postponement, or attaches it to لا ريب to mean no doubt from God even if unbelievers doubt.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: من رب العالمين متعلق بتنزيل، ففي الكلام تقديم وتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects attaching من رب العالمين to لا ريب because the intended point is absolute absence of doubt, grounded in the Quran's inimitability.
rows.anchor: وأما كونه متعلقا بلا ريب، فليس بالجيد، لأن نفي الريب عنه مطلقا هو المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rayb means doubt throughout the Quran, except in the phrase rayb al-munūn.
rows.anchor: والريب: الشك، وكذا هو في كل القرآن، إلا قوله: ريب المنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the Quran was fabricated may come from an ignorant person who has not considered the matter, an obstinate person who knows it is from God and speaks out of envy, or God's decree of misguidance.
rows.anchor: وقولهم: افتراه، كلام جاهل لم يمعن النظر، أو جاحد مستيقن أنه من عند الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the pronoun in فيه to refer to the whole proposition: there is no doubt that the Quran was sent down by the Lord of all worlds.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والضمير في فيه راجع إلى مضمون الجملة، كأنه قيل: لا ريب في ذلك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the sequence as first asserting divine revelation, then rejecting the charge of fabrication, then affirming that the Quran is truth from the Lord.
rows.anchor: أثبت أولا أن تنزيله من رب العالمين، وأن ذلك ما لا ريب فيه. ثم أضرب عن ذلك إلى قوله: أم يقولون افتراه
